messages:
sam: heads up — got a report that non-admins can trigger canary rollouts from the Console. reproducer attached.

sam: steps to repro: 1) go to A/B tests -> canary, 2) click 'Promote canary', 3) request succeeds even when user lacks canary_operator role.

sam: audit shows the action was recorded as done by a service account (svc-rollout) rather than the user.

maya: ack. which cluster/env? UI only or API too?

sam: prod, via UI. quick curl against the rollout API also returns 200 when the user's token shouldn't have permission.

andre: that smells like an authz proxy problem — maybe the end-user identity header got dropped and svc-rollout is being used to authorize. any recent RBAC refactors?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: eng-platform/main @ 1743499000 — includes PR#5829 (rbac: normalize role aliases).

liz: is there customer impact or data exposure? should we page?

sam: no data exfil reported, but ability to push canary -> full rollout and fallback policy changes is high risk. classify as potential privilege escalation.

ops-oncall: suggest immediate mitigation: flip the canary UI feature flag off, and rate-limit the API path until we patch.

maya: agree. temp mitigations: 1) disable canary_ui in prod feature flags 2) add authz check server-side on the /rollouts/promote endpoint (do not trust client).

kevin: checked KMS logs for key usage — nothing anomalous. note: KMS audit events don't have the original user principal id in them; they show the service principal. we'll need to correlate using request IDs.

andre: root cause likely PR#5829 changed role alias resolution so service accounts can be used in place of proxied user identity. authz path used role alias map which now prefers service principal. quick fix: restore previous alias precedence and assert presence of x-proxy-user header before allowing rollout actions.

sam: vuln triage: severity = high. recommended immediate actions: hotfix to enforce server-side permission gating + ensure audit logs record end-user identity + backfill missing audit entries for any promotations since 1743499000.

liz: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note in case any clients ask.

maya: action items (owners):
- flip feature flag = ops-oncall
- hotfix authz check = andre
- add and ship audit correlation id & backfill = kevin
- comms draft = liz
- incident doc + postmortem = sam

ops-oncall: feature flag flipped off at 1743500200. confirmed UI action now disabled.

andre: cutting hotfix PR now — will include unit tests and an integration test that asserts missing x-proxy-user yields 403. pinging @eng-runtime for review.

kevin: starting audit backfill job: will scan rollout events from 1743499000..now and try to reconstruct end-users using request-id correlation. ETA ~4h. will report results in INC-4257.

deploy-bot: incident ticket created INC-4257: "Canary promotion allowed by non-admin due to RBAC alias change". severity: high.

maya: estimated ETA for hotfix deploy = 2h. after deploy we'll re-enable canary feature flag in a canary-controlled rollout to make sure authz holds.

sam: good plan. please document the exact PRs and changelist ids in the incident ticket and include links to the failing e2e. also add a test in the RBAC test matrix so this can't regress.

andre: will add test and tag codeowners. cutting PR 5892 now.

liz: comms draft ready, keeping neutral language and saying we disabled canary temporarily while we validate permissions. will not mention internal svc account detail.

sam: thanks all. keep updates in INC-4257. we'll run a short postmortem after backfill completes. :thumbsup:
